title: petrobras eyes diesel price hike awaiting government measures shield consumers 2026 09 10
text:
RIO DE JANEIRO, Sept 10 (Reuters) - Brazil's Petrobras is looking to raise diesel prices ‌at its refineries by about 1 real ($0.1964) per liter, but is waiting for government measures to shield consumers from ​the increase, two sources at the state-run ​oil firm told Reuters.
The hike would help Petrobras ⁠narrow the gap between domestic diesel prices and ​international benchmarks, which has widened due to the conflict ​in the Middle East and diesel export restrictions from Russia.
Despite being a diesel producer, Brazil still imports roughly a quarter of ​its diesel demand. When Petrobras is forced to ​import fuel at higher international prices than it charges domestically, ‌the ⁠margin squeeze hurts profitability.
With a 1 real increase, the price gap would almost disappear, one source said.
The increase would be possible thanks to a new diesel subsidy ​initially set ​at 1 ⁠real per liter, to be added to an existing one of about 1.12 ​reais per liter. Details of the measure ​have ⁠yet to be unveiled, however.
Petrobras did not immediately reply to a request for comment over the price hike.
